original_question: For a general isolated hypersurface singularity in C^n defined by the germ of a holomorphic function F, the Mather-Yau theorem says that the singularity is determined up to biholomorphism by n and the isomorphism class of the Tjurina algebra T_F = C[[z_1, ..., z_n]]/(F, F_{z_1}, ..., F_{z_n}). How can one explicitly reconstruct the singularity from this Tjurina algebra?
target_in_paper: The draft is closest not to the full Mather–Yau reconstruction problem for arbitrary isolated hypersurface germs, but to the homogeneous associated-form problem surveyed in Conjecture 1.1 of arXiv:1803.04005: whether every regular GL_n-invariant on the nondegenerate degree-d forms X_n^d can be recovered as the pullback, via the associated-form morphism Φ, of a rational GL_n-invariant on the target space of associated forms. This is the paper’s paper-faithful homogeneous version of the reconstruction problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04005?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the motivating background: the Mather–Yau theorem, the role of the Tjurina algebra, and the desire for an explicit reconstruction procedure. It also correctly points toward isolated hypersurface singularities over C and toward recovering the singularity from an algebra attached to the germ. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04005?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper does not ask about arbitrary isolated hypersurface germs F in O_n = C{z_1,...,z_n} or C[[z_1,...,z_n]]; its main target is homogeneous hypersurface singularities coming from a homogeneous form f of degree d >= 3 on C^n, with n >= 2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04005?utm_source=openai))

The relevant ambient space is the vector space Q_n^d (or equivalent notation) of degree-d homogeneous forms on C^n, and one restricts to the open subset X_n^d = {f : Δ(f) != 0} of nondegenerate forms, where Δ is the discriminant. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04005?utm_source=openai))

The paper’s official formulation is not 'reconstruct the germ explicitly from T_F' directly; it is formulated via the associated-form morphism Φ from X_n^d to forms of degree n(d-2) on the dual space (equivalently, via a Macaulay inverse system of the Milnor algebra). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04005?utm_source=openai))

The algebra entering the homogeneous story is the Milnor algebra M(f) = C[z_1,...,z_n]/(f_{z_1},...,f_{z_n}); for homogeneous or more generally quasi-homogeneous singularities, Saito’s theorem identifies Milnor and Tjurina algebras, which is why this gives a route to the reconstruction problem in the homogeneous case. ([maths-people.anu.edu.au](https://maths-people.anu.edu.au/~alperj/papers/assoc_forms.pdf))

The precise conjectural quantifiers are 'for every n >= 2 and d >= 3' and 'for every regular GL_n-invariant function S on X_n^d there exists a rational GL_n-invariant function R on the target space, defined at every point of Φ(X_n^d), such that R o Φ = S'. ([rimath.saitama-u.ac.jp](https://www.rimath.saitama-u.ac.jp/research/pdf/smj31-5.pdf))

The paper is about extracting a complete system of biholomorphic invariants of homogeneous isolated hypersurface singularities from their Milnor/Tjurina algebras, not about producing one canonical defining equation for a general germ. ([maths-people.anu.edu.au](https://maths-people.anu.edu.au/~alperj/papers/assoc_forms.pdf))

Your draft omits the invariant-theoretic language that is central to the paper: regular versus rational invariants, GL_n-equivariance, and the fact that the target invariants live on degree n(d-2) forms rather than directly on local algebras. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04005?utm_source=openai))

Because the paper is homogeneous-only, it does not include the full generality of arbitrary holomorphic germs F, arbitrary Tjurina algebras T_F, or a general constructive inverse to Mather–Yau outside the quasi-homogeneous setting. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04005?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let Q_n^d be the space of homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n, with n >= 2 and d >= 3, let X_n^d = {f in Q_n^d : Δ(f) != 0} be the locus of nondegenerate forms, and let Φ : X_n^d -> Q_n^{n(d-2)*} be the associated-form morphism attached to the Milnor algebra M(f) = C[z_1,...,z_n]/(f_{z_1},...,f_{z_n}). Is it true that for every regular GL_n-invariant function S on X_n^d there exists a rational GL_n-invariant function R on Q_n^{n(d-2)*}, defined at every point of Φ(X_n^d), such that R o Φ = S? Equivalently in the paper’s motivation, can one canonically extract a complete system of biholomorphic invariants of homogeneous isolated hypersurface singularities from their Milnor algebras (hence, by Saito, from their Tjurina algebras in the homogeneous/quasi-homogeneous case) via associated forms? ([rimath.saitama-u.ac.jp](https://www.rimath.saitama-u.ac.jp/research/pdf/smj31-5.pdf))
justification: The abstract of arXiv:1803.04005 says the paper studies the associated-form morphism for homogeneous degree-d forms with nonvanishing discriminant and connects it to explicit reconstruction from the Tjurina algebra. The introduction of the closely related associated-form papers spells out the exact conjectural formulation: all GL_n-invariant regular functions on X_n^d should be obtainable by pullback along Φ from rational invariants on the space of associated forms. Those same introductions also explain why this gives the homogeneous version of the reconstruction problem: for homogeneous/quasi-homogeneous singularities, Milnor and Tjurina algebras coincide, so recovering a complete invariant system from the associated form is the paper-faithful reformulation of 'explicit reconstruction' here. Hence your draft is directionally right on motivation but substantially broader than the actual scope and wording of the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04005?utm_source=openai))
